name: Duomo di Milano
description: Milan’s iconic Gothic cathedral, famous for its spires and the golden Madonnina statue at the top.

name: Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II
description: One of the oldest shopping galleries in the world, featuring 19th-century iron and glass architecture.

name: Teatro alla Scala
description: One of the most prestigious opera houses in the world, inaugurated in 1778.

name: Castello Sforzesco
description: A medieval fortress housing several museums and art collections, including Michelangelo’s last sculpture.

name: Parco Sempione
description: Large public park behind Castello Sforzesco, ideal for walks, relaxation, and city views.

name: Santa Maria delle Grazie
description: Church housing Leonardo da Vinci’s ‘The Last Supper’, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Navigli District
description: Historic canal district known for its vibrant nightlife, restaurants, and aperitivo culture.

name: Pinacoteca di Brera
description: One of Italy’s most important art galleries, featuring masterpieces from the Renaissance.

name: Arco della Pace
description: Neoclassical triumphal arch located at the northern entrance of Parco Sempione.

name: Columns of San Lorenzo
description: Ancient Roman columns from the 2nd century, now a popular meeting point.
